h: The Waterloo Side of the South Bank
p: With such a big library of games, choosing can be half the fun. A good tip is to match the game to your group's mood. If you're celebrating, a lively action shooter gets everyone shouting. If you've got a mix of ages, a co-operative puzzle adventure means everyone has a role. And if your friends love a scare, a horror game with the haptic vest thumping away is guaranteed to get the screams going. Staff can help you choose if you're unsure.

While most visitors to the South Bank head straight for the river, there's a whole other side to the area around Waterloo station that's worth exploring. Leake Street, the tunnel running underneath the station, is a legal graffiti zone where artists are constantly painting new work on the walls. It's a colourful, ever-changing gallery, and a great photo spot.

Just south of the station, Lower Marsh is a lively street with independent shops, cafés and a market with food stalls at lunchtime. It's a great place for a cheap and tasty bite before or after your session. Theatre lovers will spot The Old Vic and the Young Vic nearby on The Cut, two famous London theatres.

A little further south, in Lambeth, you'll find the Imperial War Museum London, which tells the story of conflicts from the First World War to the present day through powerful exhibitions. It's free to visit and makes for a thought-provoking few hours. The surrounding Geraldine Mary Harmsworth Park is pleasant for a sit-down afterwards. Head back towards the river and County Hall is home to the London Dungeon and the aquarium, both easy add-ons if you want to make a full day of it.
